topic: humanoid robot supply chain: components, suppliers, actuators, sensors, batteries, semiconductors, end effectors, manufacturing, materials, trade policy

items.title: ROBO Global maps the humanoid parts stack
items.summary: A new guide from the ROBO Global Robotics and Automation Index sorts the humanoid bill of materials into three systems — a sensor-and-compute brain, a body of rotary and linear actuators with precision gearing, and an energy layer where battery weight remains the core constraint. Its takeaway for suppliers: progress leans as much on the ecosystems behind AI chips, sensors and advanced materials as on the robot makers themselves.

items.title: WUJI's Hand 2 courts robot developers at $16,000
items.summary: The five-finger hand pairs brushless direct-drive motors with fingertip force sensing and plugs into MuJoCo, Isaac Sim and ROS 2 workflows, according to WUJI Tech, with teleoperation through the Wuji Glove, Apple Vision Pro or RealSense tracking. In production at $16,000, it is pitched as a developer-friendly platform for simulation, control and AI training workflows.

items.title: GAM takes over Schaeffler's PSC precision gearbox line
items.summary: GAM Enterprises has acquired the IP and manufacturing rights to the PSC servo gearbox from Schaeffler Ultra Precision Drives, standing up GAM-Melior GmbH in Hameln, Germany to build the line; terms were not disclosed. CEO Craig Van den Avont claims the gearing, already at the core of GAM's flagship GPL units, outperforms rival servo gearboxes in high-precision motion control.

items.title: Robotera's XHAND 1 PRO packs tactile fingertips and a 25 kg grip
items.summary: The five-fingered hand weighs just 1.1 kg yet lifts up to 25 kg, with fingertip sensors reading pressure, texture and temperature and back-drivable joint motors that yield when pushed, according to Robotera. Already in production for research, teleoperation and imitation-learning work, it scores 7/10 in humanoid.guide's hands directory.

items.title: Stabilus and Synapticon pair up to mass-produce humanoid joints
items.summary: Motion-control manufacturer Stabilus and drive-tech specialist Synapticon have formed a strategic partnership to jointly develop and build integrated actuators for humanoid robots, covering joints from the head and wrists down to the hips and knees. Small-series production starts at Stabilus plants in Europe in 2027, with large-scale output planned in North America from 2028 to sit close to major humanoid makers, according to the companies.

items.title: RoboSense goes fully solid-state with its E2 robot lidar
items.summary: The Shenzhen lidar maker unveiled E2, a fully solid-state digital lidar built on its in-house SPAD-SoC that fits up to a 180-degree field of view behind just two exposed optical windows, aimed at humanoids, quadrupeds, drones and mowers, according to RoboSense. Two companion chipsets — Phoenix for long-range precision and Peacock for image-grade wide-angle 3D perception — debut alongside it, with the company counting AgiBot, Pudu Robotics and Geek+ among robotics partners already on its lidars.

items.title: TDK and LG Innotek join forces on robot eyes and skin
items.summary: The Japanese and Korean component giants have formed a strategic partnership to co-develop sensing modules for humanoids and physical AI — pairing TDK's InvenSense inertial sensors, position sensors and microphones with LG Innotek's optical and ultra-precision module design, according to the companies. Multi-sensing, says LG Innotek CEO Moon Hyuksoo, is set to become a key capability in robotics.

items.title: A robot fingertip that feels by changing color
items.summary: Researchers at Queen Mary University of London and Italian partner universities built a fingertip whose synthetic skin shifts color as it deforms, letting an embedded camera map contact pressure and surface topology at 100-micrometer resolution with zero computational latency, according to the team. The mechanochromic design could give robot hands quantitative touch without packing electronics into the fingertip, though durability in real-world use is still unproven.

items.title: Tacta shows its robot hand — and the glove that trains it
items.summary: Palo Alto's Tacta Systems unveiled TactaBot, pairing a 15-joint Tacta Hand driven by fluidic tendon actuation with a sensor-laden skill-capture glove and an AI engine trained on recorded human technique, according to the company. Tactile sensors smaller than a grain of sand read pressures from 250 to 700,000 pascals at 400 samples a second, with first deployments in electronics manufacturing slated for early 2027.

items.title: TrendForce: America owns the robot brains, China the parts
items.summary: The US dominates the intelligence stack through Nvidia, Google DeepMind and OpenAI, while China's localized servo motors, reducers and batteries give it the edge in manufacturing scale, according to TrendForce's new component supply chain influence index — which cites AgiBot going from 5,000 to 10,000 units built in just three months as proof of that scaling speed.

items.title: China ships 20% fewer magnets to the US despite the truce
items.summary: Chinese rare-earth magnet exports to the US averaged 479 tons a month in the first half of 2026, about 20% below the pre-restriction norm, according to US customs data — a squeeze that lands squarely on the permanent-magnet motors inside EVs, factory automation and humanoid actuators. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer calls Beijing's compliance "not perfect."

items.title: Mimic puts its tendon-driven Hand M1 into production
items.summary: The Swiss startup's five-fingered M1 pairs a 25 kg power grasp with tactile sensing fine enough to feel 50 grams, according to mimic — built in-house in Switzerland as part of a full-stack platform that includes a data-collection wearable. humanoid.guide's hands directory scores it 7/10.

items.title: Renesas organizes its humanoid push around four subsystem domains
items.summary: The chipmaker is structuring its humanoid strategy into brain-and-motion, sensing, actuation and power management — betting suppliers will buy platforms rather than parts in a market it expects, according to Renesas, to double every year through 2030.

items.title: Agility's six-point policy plan puts the component gap first
items.summary: CEO Peggy Johnson urges Washington to close the gap on internationally sourced parts — citing McKinsey data that China holds roughly 90% of permanent-magnet motor capacity — in Agility's recommendations for a U.S. humanoid strategy.

items.title: Robot-hand maker Tesollo starts the IPO process after its Series B
items.summary: The Incheon-based end-effector specialist — whose five-fingered DG-5F-S weighs under 1 kg and comes in at about 60% of its predecessor's cost, according to the company — exports to 19 countries and is preparing to list next year.
